enonce_intro_markdown:
A continuous random variable $X$ has probability density function, $f$, where

$$f(x) = \begin{cases} kx(3 - x), & 0 \le x \le 3 \\ 0 & \text{elsewhere.} \end{cases}$$
incertitudes: Question 4 : la troisième partie (« Show that the upper quartile, $u$, ... ») n'a pas de lettre imprimée ; elle est numérotée « c » ici. Les points imprimés (3, 7, 3) totalisent 13 ; recopiés tels quels.

Question 4 (c) : le corrigé démontre l'équation demandée à partir de $F(u) = \frac{3}{4}$ et vérifie (hors demande) que sa seule racine dans $[0, 3]$ est $u = 2.021$ (les deux autres racines, $-1.319$ et $3.798$, sont hors du domaine).

questions.enonce_markdown: Find (a) the value of the constant $k$,
questions.corrige_markdown:
A probability density function must satisfy $\displaystyle\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} f(x)\,dx = 1$, so

$$\int_0^3 kx(3 - x)\,dx = k\int_0^3 (3x - x^2)\,dx = k\left[\frac{3x^2}{2} - \frac{x^3}{3}\right]_0^3 = k\left(\frac{27}{2} - 9\right) = \frac{9k}{2}$$

Setting $\dfrac{9k}{2} = 1$ gives

**$k = \dfrac{2}{9}$.**

With $f(x) = \dfrac{2}{9}x(3 - x) = \dfrac{2}{9}(3x - x^2)$ on $[0, 3]$.

**Mean.**

$$E(X) = \int_0^3 x f(x)\,dx = \frac{2}{9}\int_0^3 (3x^2 - x^3)\,dx = \frac{2}{9}\left[x^3 - \frac{x^4}{4}\right]_0^3 = \frac{2}{9}\left(27 - \frac{81}{4}\right) = \frac{2}{9} \times \frac{27}{4} = \frac{3}{2}$$

(This agrees with the symmetry of $f$ about $x = \frac{3}{2}$.)

**Variance.** First $E(X^2)$:

$$E(X^2) = \int_0^3 x^2 f(x)\,dx = \frac{2}{9}\int_0^3 (3x^3 - x^4)\,dx = \frac{2}{9}\left[\frac{3x^4}{4} - \frac{x^5}{5}\right]_0^3 = \frac{2}{9}\left(\frac{243}{4} - \frac{243}{5}\right) = \frac{2}{9} \times \frac{243}{20} = \frac{27}{10}$$

$$\text{Var}(X) = E(X^2) - [E(X)]^2 = \frac{27}{10} - \frac{9}{4} = \frac{54 - 45}{20} = \frac{9}{20}$$

**Mean $E(X) = \dfrac{3}{2} = 1.5$; variance $\text{Var}(X) = \dfrac{9}{20} = 0.45$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Show that the upper quartile, $u$, of the distribution satisfies the equation $8u^3 - 36u^2 + 81 = 0$.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The upper quartile $u$ is the value such that $P(X \le u) = \dfrac{3}{4}$, that is $F(u) = \dfrac{3}{4}$, where $F$ is the cumulative distribution function. For $0 \le u \le 3$:

$$F(u) = \int_0^u \frac{2}{9}(3t - t^2)\,dt = \frac{2}{9}\left[\frac{3t^2}{2} - \frac{t^3}{3}\right]_0^u = \frac{2}{9}\left(\frac{3u^2}{2} - \frac{u^3}{3}\right) = \frac{u^2}{3} - \frac{2u^3}{27}$$

Setting $F(u) = \dfrac{3}{4}$:

$$\frac{u^2}{3} - \frac{2u^3}{27} = \frac{3}{4}$$

Multiply both sides by 108 (the lowest common multiple of 3, 27 and 4):

$$36u^2 - 8u^3 = 81$$

$$\boxed{8u^3 - 36u^2 + 81 = 0}$$

which is the required equation. (Numerically, its only root in $[0, 3]$ is $u \approx 2.021$; the other roots, $-1.319$ and $3.798$, lie outside $[0, 3]$.)
